325129.title: Stasinski–Voll's signed $L$-generating-function conjecture for hyperoctahedral descent classes
325129.statement:
Let $B_n$ be the hyperoctahedral group, with Coxeter length $l:B_n\to\mathbb{N}_0$ and descent set

$$
D(w)=\{i\in[n-1]_0\mid l(ws_i)<l(w)\}.
$$

For $I=\{i_1,\dots,i_l\}_{<}\subseteq[n-1]_0$, put $i_{l+1}=n$ and define

$$
B_n^{I^{\mathrm{c}}}=\{w\in B_n\mid D(w)\subseteq I\},
$$

where $I^{\mathrm{c}}=[n-1]_0\setminus I$. For $w\in B_n$, let

$$
L(w)=\frac{1}{2}\#\{(i,j)\in[\pm n]_0^2\mid i<j,\ w(i)>w(j),\ i\not\equiv j\bmod(2)\}.
$$

Writing $(\underline{m})=1-X^m$, $(\underline{0})=1$, and

$$
f_{n,I}(X)=\frac{(\underline{n})!}{(\underline{i_1})!}\prod_{r=1}^{l}\prod_{\sigma=1}^{\lfloor(i_{r+1}-i_r)/2\rfloor}(\underline{2\sigma})^{-1},
$$

**Stasinski–Voll's conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $I=\{i_1,\dots,i_l\}_{<}\subseteq[n-1]_0$,

$$
\sum_{w\in B_n^{I^{\mathrm{c}}}}(-1)^{l(w)}X^{L(w)}=f_{n,I}(X).
$$

In particular, when $I=[n-1]_0$, this asserts that the signed $L$-generating function over all of $B_n$ equals $(\underline{n})!$. The conjecture gives explicit generating functions for the new statistic $L$ on hyperoctahedral descent classes; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

325236.title: The rationality phenomenon for finite submatching events
325236.statement:
Let $\pi_0\in\textnormal{NC}_{k}$ be a finite noncrossing matching, and let $\Pi_*^{(n)}$ be the finite-size loop-percolation connectivity pattern on a system of size $n$. The event $\pi_0\mathrel{\lhd}\Pi_*^{(n)}$ is the associated submatching event.

**The rationality phenomenon for finite submatching events.** For $n\ge k$, there is an even polynomial $Q_{\pi_0}(n)$ of degree $k(k+1)$ with dyadic rational coefficients such that

$$
\mathbb{P}\left( \pi_0 \mathrel{\lhd} \Pi_*^{(n)} \right)=\frac{Q_{\pi_0}(n)}{\prod_{j=1}^{k}(4n^2-j^2)^{k+1-j}}.
$$

Moreover, $Q_{\pi_0}$ can be computed by polynomial interpolation, as in Algorithm B in Appendix A.

This gives an explicit rational dependence on the finite system size for every submatching event. The supplied text presents it as a conjectural generalization of previously established identities and does not provide a resolution.

325556.title: The branching-path conjecture for k-Schur functions
325556.statement:
Let $\mathcal C^{k+1}$ and $\mathcal C^k$ denote the sets of $(k+1)$-cores and $k$-cores, respectively. For $\lambda\in\mathcal C^{k+1}$ and $\mu\in\mathcal C^k$, let $b_{\mu\lambda}^{(k-1\to k)}(t)$ be the branching coefficient in the $k$-Schur expansion, and define

$$
b_{\mu\lambda}^{(k)}(t):=\sum_{[\mathbf p]\in\overline{\mathcal P}^{k}(\lambda,\mu)}t^{{\rm ch}(\mathbf p)},
$$

where $\overline{\mathcal P}^{k}(\lambda,\mu)$ is the relevant set of paths in the poset of $k$-shapes and ${\rm ch}(\mathbf p)$ is their charge.

**The branching-path conjecture.** For all $\lambda\in\mathcal C^{k+1}$ and $\mu\in\mathcal C^k$,

$$
b_{\mu\lambda}^{(k-1\to k)}(t)=b_{\mu\lambda}^{(k)}(t).
$$

The conjecture identifies adjacent-level branching coefficients with charge-generating functions of paths in the poset of $k$-shapes. It was stated in earlier work and is known in the specialization $t=1$, but remains unproved in the stated graded form.

325658.title: Horak–Rosa conjecture on edge-length lists of Hamiltonian paths
325658.statement:
Let $K_v$ be the complete graph on $\\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\\\}$. For an edge $[x,y]$ of $K_v$, define its length by

$$
\ell(x,y)=\min(|x-y|,v-|x-y|),
$$

and let $\ell(H)$ be the multiset of edge-lengths of a Hamiltonian path $H$. Let $L$ be a list of $v-1$ positive integers not exceeding $\lfloor v/2\rfloor$. **Horak and Rosa's conjecture.** There exists a Hamiltonian path $H$ of $K_v$ with $\ell(H)=L$ if and only if, for every sublist $J$ of $L$ satisfying $J\cap(L\setminus J)=\emptyset$,

$$
|J|\geq \gcd\\{v,\ell\mid \ell\in L\setminus J\\}-1.
$$

This generalizes Buratti's conjecture from prime order to arbitrary $v$. The paper also gives an equivalent divisor formulation in the abstract and proves the conjecture when all elements of $L$ belong to $\\{1,2,3,5\\}$; the full assertion remains open in the source.

325828.title: Faben and Jerrum's homomorphism-counting dichotomy conjecture for graphs
325828.statement:
Let $H$ be a (not necessarily simple) graph. The **involution-free reduction** of $H$ is the lexicographically minimal involution-free graph $H'$ such that $H\rightarrow^* H'$. The problem $\oplus \operatorname{HomsTo}(H)$ asks for the number of graph homomorphisms to $H$, modulo $2$.

**Faben and Jerrum's conjecture.** The problem $\oplus \operatorname{HomsTo}(H)$ is in $\mathrm{FP}$ if the involution-free reduction of $H$ is the empty graph, a singleton vertex with or without a self-loop, or a graph with two isolated vertices, exactly one of which has a self-loop. Otherwise, it is $\oplus\mathrm{P}$-complete.

This conjecture proposes a complexity dichotomy for counting graph homomorphisms modulo $2$ on arbitrary graphs, extending the known dichotomy for trees. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

325846.title: Irregular graphical Deligne–Simpson conjecture
325846.statement:
Choose a marking of each conjugacy class $\breve{\mathcal{C}}_i\subset \operatorname{GL}(V_i)$ for all $i\in I$. Gluing legs to obtain a supernova graph $\widehat{\Gamma}$ with node set $\widehat{I}$ determines parameters $q,d$ and a Kac–Moody root system in $\mathbb{Z}^{\widehat{I}}$, hence the positive roots. Let $(\,\ )$ denote the associated symmetric bilinear form, and write $q^d$ and $q^{d_i}$ for the corresponding multiplicative parameters. **Irregular graphical Deligne–Simpson conjecture.** The graphical Deligne–Simpson problem for the graph $\Gamma$ and conjugacy classes $\breve{\mathcal{C}}$ admits a solution if and only if $d$ is a positive root, $q^d=1$, and, whenever $d=d_1+d_2+\cdots$ is a nontrivial sum of positive roots with $q^{d_1}=q^{d_2}=\cdots=1$, one has

$$
\Delta(d)>\Delta(d_1)+\Delta(d_2)+\cdots,
$$

where

$$
\Delta(d)=2-(d,d).
$$

This is the proposed irregular analogue of Crawley-Boevey's criterion for the tame Deligne–Simpson problem; the tame conjecture was announced as proved, whereas the corresponding irregular criterion is presented here as a conjecture.

326090.title: Monochromatic subdiagram cover-dimension conjecture
326090.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset, let $D$ be its order diagram, let $E$ be the edge set of $D$, and let $\phi:E\to\{1,2,\dots,r\}$ be an $r$-coloring of the edges. For a subdiagram $D'$ with associated suborder $P'$, let $\dim_{uc}(D')$ and $\dim_{lc}(D')$ denote the upper- and lower-cover dimensions used in the paper. **Monochromatic subdiagram cover-dimension conjecture.** For every pair $(d,r)$ of positive integers, there is a poset $P$ with $\dim(P)=d$ such that some $\alpha\in\{1,2,\dots,r\}$ satisfies, for

$$
D'\text{ having edge set }\{e\in E:\phi(e)=\alpha\},
$$

with $P'$ the suborder determined by $D'$,

$$
\dim_{uc}(D')=\dim_{lc}(D')=\dim(P).
$$

The conjecture is presented as stronger than the preceding doubling conjecture and is intended to provide a robust monochromatic-subdiagram formulation; the supplied text gives no resolution.

326317.title: Classification conjecture for primitive regular hexagonal tilings of the integer lattice
326317.statement:
For $x\in\mathbb{Z}^2$, let $s_x=\{x_1,x_1+1\}\times\{x_2,x_2+1\}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^2$ and let $\bar{s}_x=[x_1,x_1+1]\times[x_2,x_2+1]\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$. A **tile** is a set $T$ of squares $s_x$ such that $I(T)=\bigcup_{s_x\in T}\bar{s}_x$ is a topological disk. A tiling of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is a collection of tiles in which every square $s_x$ belongs to exactly one tile. A tiling is **regular** if it has the form $T+L$ for some tile $T$ and lattice $L\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^2$, **hexagonal** if every tile borders exactly six other tiles, and **primitive** if every regular refinement is either itself or the tiling by individual squares. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be the family of circles, and for each $C\in\mathcal{B}$ let $T_C+L_C$ be the associated regular tiling by $90^\circ$-symmetric tiles.

**Classification conjecture.** If $\mathcal{T}$ is a primitive, regular, hexagonal tiling of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ by $90^\circ$-symmetric tiles, then

$$
\mathcal{T}=T_C+L_C+v
$$

for some $C\in\mathcal{B}$ and some $v\in\mathbb{Z}^2$.

The claim predicts that the circle construction accounts for all primitive regular hexagonal tilings of the integer lattice with the stated rotational symmetry. The supplied text does not establish the classification or indicate whether it has been resolved.

326685.title: Necessity of the polarization-preservation condition for $I[S](P)$
326685.statement:
Let $P$ be a linear multiple-access channel with associated family of subspaces $\mathcal{V}$, let $S$ be a subset of the input coordinates, and let $\operatorname{proj}_S$ denote projection onto the coordinates in $S$. The quantity $I[S](P)$ is preserved by the polarization process only if there exists a subspace $V_S$ of dimension $|S|$ such that

$$
\operatorname{proj}_S(V_S)=\mathbb{F}_q^S,
$$

and, for every $V\in\mathcal{V}$,

$$
\operatorname{proj}_S(V_S\cap V)=\operatorname{proj}_S(V).
$$

**Necessity conjecture for preservation of $I[S](P)$.** If $I[S](P)$ is preserved by the polarization process, then such a subspace $V_S$ must exist. The condition is presented as necessary for preservation, not as a sufficient condition. The surrounding result establishes sufficiency under the same condition, while this statement records the converse necessity.

326761.title: Positivity conjecture for fused multi-state ASEP update matrices
326761.statement:
Let $M_{i,i+1}^{(\ell)}$ be the update matrix

$$
M_{i,i+1}^{(\ell)}=\sum_{r=1}^{\ell}b_r^{(\ell)}M_{i,i+1}^{(\ell;r)}.
$$

Normalize $b_r^{(\ell)}=\begin{bmatrix}\ell\\r\end{bmatrix}\widetilde b_r^{(\ell)}$, where

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\frac{[x]!}{[x-y]![y]!},\qquad [x]!=[x][x-1]\cdots[1],\qquad [x]=\frac{q^x-q^{-x}}{q-q^{-1}}.
$$

Because the update matrix is symmetric under $q\leftrightarrow q^{-1}$, take $0\leq q\leq1$. **Positivity conjecture.** The positivity conditions obtained from the matrix elements $\langle0|\otimes\langle r+x|M_{i,i+1}^{(\ell)}|r\rangle\otimes|x\rangle$, with $r=1,\dots,\ell-x$ and $x=0,\dots,\ell-1$, are

$$
(-1)^{r-1}\widetilde b_r^{(\ell)}>0,
$$

and

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{s}q^{(s-1)k}\begin{bmatrix}s\\k\end{bmatrix}\widetilde b_{k+i}^{(\ell)}(-1)^{i-1}>0,
\qquad i=1,\dots,\ell-s,
$$

for $s=1,\dots,\ell-1$. This conjecture gives the parameter restrictions ensuring positivity of the arbitrary linear combination of fused Temperley–Lieb generators and hence the existence of the corresponding multi-state ASEP for arbitrary $\ell$.

327010.title: The transfinite columns property conjecture
327010.statement:
Let $A$ be an $\omega\times\omega$ matrix with entries from $\mathbb Z$, and assume that $A$ is partition regular. A matrix has **bounded row sums** when the sums of the absolute values of the entries in its rows are bounded. Writing the columns as $\langle\vec c_i\rangle_{i<\omega}$, $A$ has the **transfinite columns property** if there are a countable ordinal $\mu$ and a partition $\langle I_\sigma\rangle_{\sigma<\mu}$ of $\omega$ such that

$$
\sum_{i\in I_0}\vec c_i=\vec 0
$$

and, for every $t\in\mu\setminus\{0\}$, $\sum_{i\in I_t}\vec c_i$ is a rational linear combination of $\{\vec c_i:i\in\bigcup_{j<t}I_j\}$.

**Transfinite columns property conjecture.** If $A$ has bounded row sums, then $A$ has the transfinite columns property.

This is proposed as a weaker substitute for the bounded-row-sums columns property conjecture. The paper notes that matrices can require arbitrarily large countable ordinals in this transfinite condition, and leaves the proposed statement open.

327561.title: Codimension-one connectedness conjecture for associated graphs
327561.statement:
Let $X$ be an irreducible Harish-Chandra $(\mathfrak{g},K)$-module, and let

$$
\operatorname{\mathcal{AV}}(X)=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\ell}\overline{\mathbb{O}^K_i}
$$

be the irreducible decomposition of its associated variety. The graph $\operatorname{\mathcal{AV}^\Gamma}(X)$ has these irreducible components as vertices, with edges inherited from the orbit graph: two vertices are joined when the intersection of their closures contains a nilpotent $K$-orbit of codimension one. **Codimension-one connectedness conjecture.** The graph $\operatorname{\mathcal{AV}^\Gamma}(X)$ is connected. Equivalently, for every pair $(\mathbb{O}^K_i,\mathbb{O}^K_j)$, there is a sequence

$$
\mathbb{O}^K_i=\mathbb{O}^K_{i_0},\;\mathbb{O}^K_{i_1},\;\mathbb{O}^K_{i_2},\;\dots,\;\mathbb{O}^K_{i_n}=\mathbb{O}^K_j
$$

such that, for $1\leq k\leq n$, $\overline{\mathbb{O}^K_{i_{k-1}}}\cap\overline{\mathbb{O}^K_{i_k}}$ contains a nilpotent $K$-orbit of codimension one. The conjecture concerns the codimension-one connectedness of irreducible components of associated varieties of Harish-Chandra modules. Vogan's theorem shows that the boundary of each component has codimension one when the associated variety is reducible, but the boundary may have components that do not connect distinct $K$-orbits. The general connectedness assertion remains open, and the source allows $K$ to be disconnected.

327606.title: The injective Yamanouchi-word conjecture for dual equivalence components
327606.statement:
Let $b4$ be a diagram with $n$ cells. Write $a3am(n)$ for the set of standard Yamanouchi words of length $n$, $a3am_b4(n)$ for the subset associated with $b4$, and let $c1$ denote the signature map on the components of $bca_b4$. For a component $c2=(V,c1,E)$ of $bca_b4$, let $F_{c1(v)}(X)$ be the fundamental quasisymmetric function indexed by the signature of $v$. **The injective Yamanouchi-word conjecture.** There exists an injective function

$$
f_b4\colon \operatorname{SYam}(n)\hookrightarrow S_n
$$

fixing $a3am_b4(n)$ and preserving $c1$ such that, for every component $c2=(V,c1,E)$ of $bca_b4$,

$$
\sum_{v\in V} F_{c1(v)}(X)=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\left|\left\{c0\in\operatorname{SYam}(\lambda):f_b4(c0)\in V\right\}\right|s_\lambda.
$$

This would give a Schur-positive expansion for the quasisymmetric functions associated with all components of $bca_b4$, by encoding their vertices through Yamanouchi words and Schur multiplicities.

328607.title: Truncated hook-length and restricted colored-partition linear-term conjecture
328607.statement:
Let $[...]$ range over partitions of $n$, let $h_{ij}$ be the hook length of the cell $(i,j)$, and fix $m$. Define the truncated hook-length expression

$$
H_{n,m}(b)=\sum_{\lambda \vdash n}\prod_{\substack{h_{ij}\in\lambda\\h_{ij}\leq m}}\left(1-\frac{b}{h_{ij}^2}\right).
$$

Define the restricted colored-partition series

$$
C_{1-b,m}^{\prime}(q)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q^n\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\prod_{\lambda_j\geq1}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\binom{1-b}{i+1}\binom{\min(\lambda_j,m)-1}{i}\right)
$$

and equivalently

$$
C_{1-b,m}^{\prime}(q)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q^n\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\prod_{\lambda_j\geq1}\left(1-b\right)\cdots\left(1-\frac{b}{\min(\lambda_j,m)}\right).
$$

**Truncated hook-length conjecture.** For every $n$ and fixed $m$, the linear terms in $b$ of $H_{n,m}(b)$ and the coefficient of $q^n$ in $C_{1-b,m}^{\prime}(q)$ are equal.
The conjecture is motivated by numerical agreement for the 3- and 4-truncations. The paper notes that the relationship may admit a better formulation and that a correction term for unmodified truncations remains to be determined.

329099.title: Equitable partition conjecture for prescribed block sizes
329099.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $s^{n,k}=\frac{1}{k}\binom{n+1}{2}$ be an integer, and let a partition of $[n]$ **implement** $\{p_i\}_{i=1}^k$ when its blocks can be bijectively matched with the prescribed sizes $p_1,\ldots,p_k$. Call a partition **equitable** when every block has sum $s^{n,k}$. Let $k<n$ be positive integers, let $1<p_1\leqslant p_2\leqslant\cdots\leqslant p_k$ with $\sum_{i=1}^k p_i=n$, and set $P_j=\sum_{i=1}^j p_i$. **Equitable partition conjecture.** There exists an equitable partition of $[n]$ implementing $\{p_i\}_{i=1}^k$ if and only if

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{P_j}(n-i+1)\geqslant j s^{n,k}
$$

for every $j=1,\ldots,k$. This conjecture asserts sufficiency of the stated necessary condition for equal-sum partitions with prescribed block sizes; the supplied source gives no resolution evidence.

330062.title: The inv-maj bijection for fillings and conjugate partition shapes
330062.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the set of all fillings of Young diagrams with positive integers. For a filling $\sigma$, let $\operatorname{inv}(\sigma)$ and $\operatorname{maj}(\sigma)$ denote its inversion and major-index statistics, let $\mathcal{F}_\mu^\alpha$ be the fillings of shape $\mu$ and content $\alpha$, and write $\mathcal{F}_\mu^\alpha|_{\operatorname{inv}=a,\operatorname{maj}=b}$ for those with the indicated statistic values. **The inv-maj bijection conjecture.** There is a natural isomorphism of weighted sets

$$
\varphi:(\mathcal{F};\operatorname{inv},\operatorname{maj})\to(\mathcal{F};\operatorname{maj},\operatorname{inv})
$$

which interchanges $\operatorname{inv}$ and $\operatorname{maj}$ and sends a partition shape to its conjugate; equivalently, for every $a,b,\mu,\alpha$, it restricts to a bijection

$$
\varphi:\mathcal{F}_\mu^\alpha|_{\operatorname{inv}=a,\operatorname{maj}=b}\to\mathcal{F}_{\mu^\ast}^\alpha|_{\operatorname{inv}=b,\operatorname{maj}=a}.
$$

This would provide an elementary combinatorial proof of the $q,t$-symmetry relation for transformed Macdonald polynomials, extending the classical inv-maj equidistribution on permutations. The source does not state a resolution.

330646.title: The quasi-isomorphism conjecture for arithmetic graphs and the plaid model
330646.statement: Let $p/q$ be the rational parameter, let $Gamma(p/q)$ be its arithmetic landscape, and let $T_{p/q}$ be the affine map carrying the plaid model's fundamental domain to the arithmetic graph's fundamental domain. Consider the polygons of $T_{p/q}^{-1}(\Gamma_{p/q})$ and the polygons of the plaid model in their respective fundamental domains. **Quasi-isomorphism conjecture.** There is a bijection between these two polygon sets such that each polygon in one model lies within a $2$-tubular neighborhood of its corresponding polygon in the other. This conjecture asserts that the arithmetic graph and plaid model have the same coarse polygonal geometry, up to a uniformly bounded discrepancy; the surrounding discussion presents it as the speculative correspondence underlying the relationship between special outer-billiards orbits and the plaid model.

331778.title: The separability characterization of matching-stable graphs
331778.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected non-bipartite graph. A matching queue $(G,lambda,Phi)_{scriptsize{\textsc{c}}}$ has arrival-rate vector $lambda$ in $textsc{Ncond}_{scriptsize{\textsc{c}}}(G)$, where $Phi$ is an admissible matching policy. A graph is **matching-stable** if the corresponding matching queue is stable for every admissible matching policy and every arrival-rate vector satisfying this condition. A graph is **separable** if it has the separability property used in the paper, and its order is the number of vertices in the relevant separable component.

**Separability characterization conjecture.** The only connected and non-bipartite graphs $G$ for which the matching queue $(G,\lambda,\Phi)_{\scriptsize{\textsc{c}}}$ is stable for any admissible matching policy $\Phi$ and any $\lambda \in \textsc{Ncond}_{\scriptsize{\textsc{c}}}(G)$ are the separable graphs of order $3$ or more.

The conjecture would extend the paper's characterization from the complement of the class of graphs inducing an odd cycle of size at least $7$ without a $5$-cycle or pendant graph. Equivalently, since graphs in that remaining class are non-separable, it asserts that no such graph is matching-stable; the paper reports that this remains unproved and identifies instability for the pendant graph and the $5$-cycle as supporting results.

331994.title: Multi-separation star refinement conjecture

340112.title: Kawarabayashi–Ozeki conjecture on disjoint paths preserving connectivity
340112.statement:
Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers. A graph is **$r$-connected** if deleting fewer than $r$ vertices leaves it connected. For a graph $G$ and paths $P_1,\ldots,P_k$, write $G-\bigcup_{i=1}^k V(P_i)$ for the graph obtained by deleting all vertices on those paths.

**Kawarabayashi–Ozeki conjecture.** There exists a function $f(k,l)$ such that, for every $f(k,l)$-connected graph $G$ and two distinct vertices $s$ and $t$ in $G$, there are $k$ internally disjoint paths $P_1,\ldots,P_k$ with endpoints $s$ and $t$ such that

$$
G-\bigcup_{i=1}^k V(P_i)
$$

is $l$-connected.

This conjecture strengthens the cited result that, after deleting one induced path between two specified vertices from a sufficiently highly connected graph, the remainder can be required to be $k$-connected. It asks whether a bounded connectivity assumption likewise permits deleting several internally disjoint $s$–$t$ paths while retaining prescribed connectivity.
